raw.quick_summary: The example traces the recursive call S(4): calls descend to the base case S(0), which returns 0, and then results unwind upward as each caller adds its own n. The final result is 10, and each returned value belongs to its immediate caller.

key_concepts.explanation: S(n) calls S(n-1) until the bounded invocation reaches S(0). For S(4), the calls are S(4), S(3), S(2), S(1), and S(0).
S(0) returns 0 without making another recursive call.
After the base case completes, each waiting caller receives its child’s numeric result and adds its own n before returning.
Each child result is returned to exactly its immediate caller; a waiting caller cannot complete before receiving that result.
Each invocation has its own frame identity, even though all invocations use the same procedure S.
The returned values are 0 from S(0), 1 from S(1), 3 from S(2), 6 from S(3), and 10 from S(4).

learning_path.title: Tracing Recursive Calls and Returns in S(4)
learning_path.reason: The example supports a short lesson that follows the actual call-stack process from descent through unwinding.

steps.title: Trace the descending calls
steps.learning_goal: Identify the order in which recursive invocations are entered.
steps.explanation: Starting at S(4), each nonzero invocation calls the next smaller argument, producing S(4) → S(3) → S(2) → S(1) → S(0). Each invocation has its own frame.
steps.connection_to_previous: This establishes the call-stack state before any result can be returned.

steps.title: Recognize the stopping condition
steps.learning_goal: Explain why recursion stops at S(0).
steps.explanation: S(0) is the base invocation. It returns 0 immediately and does not make another recursive call.
steps.connection_to_previous: Once the descending calls reach S(0), the recursion has a defined completion point.

steps.title: Follow result ownership during unwinding
steps.learning_goal: Track how each result returns to its immediate caller.
steps.explanation: S(1) receives 0 and returns 1; S(2) receives 1 and returns 3; S(3) receives 3 and returns 6. Each caller waits for its child and then adds its own argument.
steps.connection_to_previous: The base result provides the first value that can move back up the waiting call chain.

steps.title: Complete the root invocation
steps.learning_goal: Compute the final result of S(4).
steps.explanation: S(4) receives 6 from S(3), adds 4, and returns 10. The root cannot complete before the entire child chain has returned.
steps.connection_to_previous: The final unwinding step applies the same rule at the root invocation.

checkpoint_questions.question: Which invocation is entered last during the descending phase of S(4)?
checkpoint_questions.explanation: Each nonzero call invokes the next smaller argument, so S(0) is reached last during descent.

checkpoint_questions.question: What value does S(3) return after receiving the result from S(2)?
checkpoint_questions.explanation: S(2) returns 3, and S(3) adds 3 to that child result, returning 6.

checkpoint_questions.question: Why can S(4) not complete immediately after entering?

options.text: It must create a second procedure before returning.
It must wait for S(3) to return before adding 4.
It must return the base value 0 directly.
It must reuse the same frame as S(3).

checkpoint_questions.explanation: S(4) waits for its immediate child S(3), then adds 4 to the returned value.
